desc: Read the input values $N, M, K$, the edges, and the sequences $A$ and $B$.
Construct the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of the graph using Kruskal's algorithm (sort edges by weight and use DSU to select edges).

Initialize a DSU structure to manage connected components of the MST, and for each component, maintain the count of unmatched $A$ indices and unmatched $B$ indices currently residing in that component.
Iterate through the edges of the MST in increasing order of weight. For each edge connecting components $C_1$ and $C_2$ with weight $w$:
Calculate the number of new pairs that can be formed: $cnt = \min(\text{count}_A(C_1), \text{count}_B(C_2)) + \min(\text{count}_A(C_2), \text{count}_B(C_1))$.
Add $cnt \times w$ to the total answer.

Update the counts for the merged component: $\text{count}_A(C_{new}) = \text{count}_A(C_1) + \text{count}_A(C_2) - (\text{matched from } C_1 \to C_2) - (\text{matched from } C_2 \to C_1)$, and similarly for $B$.
Print the final calculated minimum sum.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
